SMWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from  Suwannee River to Keaton Beach out 20 NM...

* Until 700 PM EST.

* At 501 PM EST, a strong thunderstorm was located 16 nm northwest
of Suwannee River. The strong thunderstorm was nearly stationary.
The Horseshoe Beach weatherstem recently gusted to 32 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots...suddenly higher
waves...frequent lightning...and heavy downpours. Make
sure all on board are wearing life jackets.

* Locations impacted include...
Horseshoe Beach and Suwannee River.
properties.instruction: Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

properties.description:

Atlantic Waters of Puerto Rico and USVI from 10 NM to 19.5N...
Coastal Waters of Northern Puerto Rico out 10 NM...

* At 542 PM AST, Doppler radar indicated a strong thunderstorm,
capable of producing winds to around 30 knots. This a strong
thunderstorm was located over the coastal waters from Hatillo to
Aguadilla, moving northwest at 5 knots.

Locations impacted include...
Mainly open waters of Atlantic Waters of Puerto Rico and USVI from
10 NM to 19.5N and Coastal Waters of Northern Puerto Rico out 10
NM.
properties.instruction:

agency. They will relay your report to the National Weather Service
office.

waves, lightning strikes, and heavy downpours. Boaters should seek
safe harbor immediately until this storm passes.

Intense lightning is occurring with this storm. If caught on the open
water stay below deck if possible, keep away from ungrounded metal
objects.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued November 20 at 4:30PM EST by NWS State College PA
properties.description:
The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection has
issued a Code ORANGE Air Quality Alert on Saturday for the
Susquehanna Valley.

A Code ORANGE Air Quality Alert means that air pollution
concentrations within the region may become unhealthy for
sensitive groups. Sensitive groups include children, people
suffering from asthma, heart disease or other lung diseases,
and the elderly. The effects of air pollution can be minimized
by avoiding strenuous activity or exercise outdoors.

For more information on ground-level ozone and fine particles,
visit www.airnow.gov, and www.aqpartners.state.pa.us.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 20 at 12:26PM PST until November 26 at 2:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, High astronomical tides
will cause minor flooding in low lying areas around Humboldt
Bay. Up to one half foot of saltwater inundation above ground
level is possible near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the
Coastal Flood Watch, High astronomical tides and large surf may
cause major flooding in low lying areas along the
Redwood/Mendocino Coast. Up to 2.5 to 3 feet of saltwater
inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways during the highest tides if
storm impacts such as strong southerly winds and large surf
arrive during high tide periods.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County, especially for areas in
and around Humboldt Bay.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 7 AM to 10 AM PST
Saturday with high tide at 8:31 AM on Saturday at the Humboldt
Bay North Spit tide gauge. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from
Sunday morning through Thursday afternoon. High tide is at
9:06 AM on Sunday, 9:44 AM on Monday, 10:25 AM on Tuesday,
11:09 AM on Wednesday, 11:56 AM on Thursday, 12:48 AM on
Friday at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater
inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high
tide.

* IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying
property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated.
Some shoreline erosion may occur.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Watch means that flooding is possible but not
imminent. Coastal residents in the watch area should begin
preparations for rising water and take appropriate action to
protect life and property.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

properties.areaDesc: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Mayaguez and Vicinity
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 20 at 4:26PM AST until November 21 at 6:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...High Rip Current Risk, life-threatening rip current.

* WHERE...From Rincon to Fajardo

* WHEN...Through Saturday afternoon

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to
10 feet with dangerous rip currents. High surf will likely
continue much of next week, peaking on Wednesday and Thursday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal flooding expected.
For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding
possible.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County
Central Coast Beaches. Impacts highest across west to northwest-
facing beaches, including Morro Bay, Pismo Beach, Oceano Dunes,
as well as the Cayucos, Pismo, and Avila Piers.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 3 PM PST this
afternoon. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM Monday to
3 AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late
Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of
sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas,
especially around the time of high tide, including over
beaches, roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is
possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest risk likely Wednesday and Thursday
with potential for significant impacts. Additional products will
likely be needed into Friday.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Plan
for extra travel time as some roads may be closed.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued November 20 at 12:03PM PST until November 22 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Portland OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Rough bar conditions expected. Seas 7 to 12 ft at 14
seconds and southeast winds 10 to 20 kt with gusts up to 25 kt
expected.

* WHERE...In the Main Channel of the Columbia River Bar.

* WHEN...From 4 AM Saturday to 4 AM PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft,
especially when operating near to, or attempting to cross, the
Columbia River Bar.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Ebb current of 4.59 kt at 110 PM Friday.
Seas 7 to 6 ft. Ebb current of 3.26 kt at 123 AM Saturday. Seas
7 to 6 ft. Ebb current of 5.44 kt at 154 PM Saturday. Seas 10
ft.
properties.instruction:
A Small Craft Advisory means that wave conditions are expected to
be hazardous to small craft in the vicinity of the Columbia River
Bar. Mariners are advised to obtain the latest bar conditions
from the United States Coast Guard before attempting to cross the
bar.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 20 at 1:00PM MST until November 24 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release continues.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...
Northeastern Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 100 PM MST, water releases from Painted Rock Dam continue with
flow peaking around 3000 cfs. A streamflow gauge immediately
downstream also indicated a stage near 10 feet.
- Flooding is expected along the Gila River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 20 at 2:35PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall has maintained a steady climb into Moderate Flood
Stage on the St Johns River at Deland, with river levels forecast to
continue climbing through this weekend. The river is anticipated to
reach Major Flood Stage on Saturday.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and
marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM EST Friday the stage was 4.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:30 PM EST Friday was 4.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 6.0 feet Tuesday
evening. Additional rises are possible thereafter. This
approaches the flood of record which is 6.3 feet.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 245 AM EST.

Fish Camp.

properties.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 20 at 10:56AM PST until November 24 at 4:00AM PST by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal
flooding possible.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM Sunday to 4 AM
PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from 4 AM PST Tuesday
through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Morning high tides will be on the increase
next week, exceeding 7 feet by Sunday. Highest tides will be
Tuesday through Thursday, peaking Wednesday. Daily high tides
each morning on Tuesday through Thursday will reach 7.9-8.2
feet. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 3-5
feet through Wednesday, but an incoming swell Wednesday into
Thursday could bring notably higher surf beginning on Thursday.
NOTE: Tides have been adjusted above baseline astronomical
predictions based on trends in recent observations.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 20 at 10:40AM PST until November 21 at 11:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.4 ft of
inundation above ground level is likely in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Bayshore locations along the San Franciso and San Pablo
Bays.

* WHEN...Until 11 AM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 8:15 AM
Saturday. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific
Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively. The
Pacific Coast will likely be added to the Advisory as early as
Sunday with the San Francisco and San Pablo Bays upgraded to a
Coastal Flood Warning as we approach "King Tides".

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of

* WHERE...The Wasatch Mountains.

* WHEN...Until 11 AM MST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Winter driving conditions are expected. Roads, and
especially bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and
hazardous.
properties.instruction:

vehicle in case of an emergency. For winter road conditions from the
Utah Department of Transportation, visit
http://www.udottraffic.utah.gov.

Persons should delay all travel if possible. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution and be prepared for sudden
changes in visibility. Leave plenty of room between you and the
motorist ahead of you, and allow extra time to reach your
destination. Avoid sudden braking or acceleration, and be especially
cautious on hills or when making turns. Make sure your car is
winterized and in good working order.

For graphical depictions of the snowfall forecast, including Official
NWS Forecast, High End Amount, and Low End Amount, visit
weather.gov/slc/winter.

properties.description:
The officials at the Indiana Department of Environmental Management
have declared a Local Air Quality Advisory, IN EFFECT FROM 6 PM THIS
EVENING TO 10 AM EST SATURDAY and 6 PM SATURDAY TO 10 AM EST SUNDAY.

A Local Air Quality Advisory for PM2.5 has been issued. Fine
particulate levels are expected to be in the Unhealthy for Sensitive
Groups range. Active children and adults, and people with
respiratory disease, such as asthma should limit prolonged outdoor
exposure.

Due to observed and forecasted high concentration of PM2.5 readings
in the area, recommendations are for the public to reduce or avoid
exertion or heavy work outdoors and keep windows and doors
closed as much as possible.

For additional information, please visit the IDEM Smog page at:

http://www.in.gov/idem/airmonitoring/smogwatch/
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.description:
The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection has issued a
Code ORANGE Air Quality Alert for Friday, for the Mon Valley area.

A code ORANGE air quality alert means that air pollution
concentrations within the region may become unhealthy for sensitive
groups. Sensitive groups include children, the elderly, and people
suffering from asthma, heart disease, or other lung diseases. The
effects of air pollution can be minimized by avoiding outdoor
exercise or strenuous activity.

For more information on ground-level ozone and fine particles, visit
http://www.airnow.gov and https://www.ahs.dep.pa.gov/AQPartnersWeb/
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.areaDesc: Elkhart
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued November 20 at 10:31AM EST by NWS Northern Indiana
properties.description:
The officials at the Indiana Department of Environmental Management
have declared a Local Air Quality Advisory for Elkhart County, in
effect from 6 PM Saturday November 21st to 10 AM EST Sunday November
22nd.

A Local Air Quality Advisory for PM 2.5 has been issued. Fine
particulate levels are expected to be in the Unhealthy for Sensitive
Groups range. Active children and adults, and people with
respiratory disease, such as asthma should limit prolonged outdoor
exposure.

Due to observed and forecasted high concentration of PM2.5 readings
in the area, recommendations are for the public to reduce or avoid
exertion or heavy work outdoors and keep windows and doors closed as
much as possible.

For additional information, please visit the IDEM Smog page at:

http://www.in.gov/idem/airmonitoring/smogwatch/
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 20 at 10:23AM EST until November 20 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of east central Florida, including the following
areas, Coastal Volusia, Inland Northern Brevard, Inland Volusia,
Mainland Northern Brevard and Northern Brevard Barrier Islands.

* WHEN...Until 7 PM EST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Extensive street flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers are
possible. Area creeks and streams are running high and could flood
with more heavy rain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Showers will continue to move onshore across Volusia county with
the threat for additional flooding through late afternoon.
Additional rainfall amounts up to 2 to 4 inches are possible.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 20 at 1:46AM CST until November 20 at 6:00PM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 PM CST this
evening. For the High Rip Current Risk, through this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching
or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles,
except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will
be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations
north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach
erosion is expected. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Volusia; Coastal Indian River; Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 20 at 12:58AM EST until November 22 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents and
rough surf. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of
5 to 12 feet in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday evening.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM EST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.
